# Review (pass 1) — hammurabi-laws-185-194

Reviewer: strongest model, adversarial. units.json edited in place by script (backup in the scratchpad). 34 units, 197 words, unchanged in count; no sign added. Not run: build, validate, publish; nothing committed. Unit numbers are 0-based positions in `sentences`, with the first stele line.

## Counts
Changes: 17 entries (high 0, medium 6, low 11).

## Plate work (Plates 55–57, PDF 325, 327, 329; Harper's List of Signs nos. 3, 4, 5, 13, 41, 70, 72, 76, 105, 138)
Not done: a stroke-level identification of every syllabogram of every row; I confirmed the group counts and the shape of the logograms and of the disputed signs below, and read the plate for the repeated words.
Drafter's flagged items:
1. **ṣi (XXXII 32 etc.)** — plate sign is Harper's no. 72 (barred box + hooked upright), distinct from no. 41 zi (zi-ik-ru-um, XXXII 52). Kept ZI (only ṣi key; same as the published part); note says so.
2. **bí-zu box sign (XXXII 80)** — the sign has a single wedge in the box and no vertical grid: it is Harper's no. 3 ba (cf. a-ba-šu XXXII 44), not no. 4 zu (grid; cf. XXXII 58, 85). Changed to BA with tr `ba(=zu)` (carver's-slip pattern of the earlier parts). The -ssu analysis stays on the grammar.
3. **SU/ŠU/ZU** — resolved to a degree: ŠU (no. 138) is a box of horizontal bars with a vertical, as in a-ba-šu XXXII 44, ŠU at XXXIII 8 and ir-ku-šu XXXIII 38; ZU and SU (nos. 4, 5) are a box with a wedge and a vertical grid (XXXII 58, 85, XXXIII 9, 40). So inakkisū (su) and uštāḫissu, rīqūssu (zu) are right as keyed, irkusu has a ŠU on the plate (noted). ZU versus SU themselves are not distinguishable at this scale. Not every -šu in the part was re-examined; the several rows looked at agree.
4. **XXXIII 6–7** — each is a single row on the plate (about 5–6 and 8 groups); no second tier. The note that both stand on two tiers was wrong; corrected. Words and line division unaffected.
5. **NER.SE.GA** — three signs confirmed (line 50, 96, XXXIII 10); the tall chevron tree is Harper's no. 76 se, and differs from ZI (no. 41); key SHE kept, still UNCERTAIN. mār-ummâni (no. 70) confirms DUMU + UM.MI.A; no. 13 confirms EME; no. 105 resembles the UBUR group at XXXIII 39.
6. XXXII 85 RI KU ZU: the final sign is the gridded box, as keyed.

## Refused or kept
- NER.SE.GA (SHE key), zikrum class, iṣīrma, uwaddīma, irtakas, mušēniqtum, UBUR as key: kept, UNCERTAIN in notes; no better reading from permitted sources.
- rīqūssu: kept UNCERTAIN; the drafter's honest remark on how it arrived stays in notes.
- `ilqēma` vs `iṣīrma`, `irtašima`, `uwaddīma` (-i + ma spelt e/i/ī unevenly): follows the published parts' convention for ilqēma and the drafter's others; not unified (owner's list).
- "he/she shall give … ittalak" etc.: kept.
- `l` of U5, U12, U14 (ša-clause relative left out of `i`): acknowledged in the note; kept.
- Remembered English in `i`: none recognised. q not ḳ: confirmed.
- `ib-ba-qar` (XXXII 59, one g in Harper) kept as printed.

Every reading reconstructs from glyph tr (including the new É-ba(=zu)); line division 106 lines unchanged; no ḳ.

# Review (pass 2) — hammurabi-laws-185-194

Reviewer: strongest model, adversarial; units.json and gloss.json edited in place by script (backups in the scratchpad). Second full pass over all 34 units (grammar labels, l and i, remembered English, house renderings, q, pass-1 changes) and over every gloss.json entry. Not committed, not published.

## Counts
Changes: 23 entries (high 0, medium 6, low 17). Refused: 6.

Checked and found sound: mārūtum, tarbītum, ummiānum, NER.SE.GA (signs only, no reading), edûm-D, ṣiārum, atta (masc./fem.), lišānum (KA × ME is the Unicode name), mušēniqtum, tulûm; broaden entries for baqārum-N, târum, izuzzum, ekallum, šiprum, qātum, manûm-count, epēšum, nasāḫum, kânum-D. No invented modern forms found; every UNCERTAIN carries its flag.

## Refused or kept
- É-ba(=zu) at XXXII 80 (pass-1 change): looked again at the plate (Plate LVI, zoom 8). The box after É has one large wedge and no grid; kept as BA with tr ba(=zu). Whether slip or autograph is imperfect stays UNCERTAIN in the note.
- "ittalak, an order after -ma" (U18): kept; the form is the perfect and the sense is plain; note already says so.
- "ša-clause relative left out of i" (U11, U14): kept, the note says so.
- "tulê rendered singular": kept (drafter's open question); the note says the form looks plural. "breasts" refused: the law's penalty is for one woman, and the Akkadian is a body-word plural.
- "iṣīrma" and "uwaddīma", "irtakas", NER.SE.GA, zikrum: kept UNCERTAIN, no better reading from permitted sources.
- "mūzaz ekallim … in the palace's service": kept; "stands (in service)" is the published izuzzum entry's wording.
- murabbīssu after ummam without the accusative vowel: kept as Harper's spelling (noted).
- Remembered English in i: none recognised after a second pass; verbal forms were rebuilt from l. q not ḳ: confirmed by script (no ḳ in units.json or gloss.json).

## Build and validate
`R3 build hammurabi hammurabi-laws-185-194`: BUILT, 34 units; one WARN (16 stele lines differ from Harper's transliteration, see linecheck.md).
`R3 validate hammurabi hammurabi-laws-185-194`: same WARN, then PASS.

## Linecheck lines confirmed on the plate
Plate LVI (PDF 327) zoom 6–8: XXXII 80 (É + box sign, see above), XXXII 85 (six sign-groups: DUMU, ŠU, U₂, RI, KU, ZU; Harper's tal is the sign also read ri), XXXII 93 (ù + É only; the row is short, no tim). Plate LVII (PDF 329) zoom 2.5: XXXIII 8 (EME + ŠU, two clusters, the ŠU at the right edge), XXXIII 39 (a large UBUR group and ŠA), group counts of XXXIII 12, 26. Confirmed in pass 1 (and not contradicted now): XXXII 52 (SAL for zinništi), 54 (DUMU + UM.MI.A), 92 (A.ŠÀ-lim, kirêm). The rest of the 16 (XXXII 70, 81; XXXIII 1, 11, 32, 37) are DUMU{meš}, DUMU or zikrum/SAL lines that Harper writes as the Akkadian word; matched by group count only, not stroke by stroke.
